header:
Co(Salen) Oxygen Carrier
Many proteins containing transition-metal ions can bind molecular oxygen to form complexes and reversibly take up and release oxygen for biological processes. Examples include the iron-containing proteins myoglobin and hemoglobin and the copper-containing protein hemocyanin. The Co-Schiff-base complex [Co(II)(Salen)], cobalt N,N'-ethylenebis(salicylideneiminate), is an important representative synthetic model oxygen carrier.

The Salen ligand coordinates Co tetradentately through 2 phenoxide O atoms and 2 imine N atoms. The benzene rings are drawn in alternating-single-and-double-bond Kekulé form, both C=N bonds are double bonds, and the central Co atom is represented as four-coordinate by the ring-closure labels [Co]34. subquestions.text_open:
6.1 Depending on the preparation method, [Co(II)(Salen)] can exist in two solid forms: dark-red, gelatinous, active form A and dark-red, crystalline, inactive form B. A rapidly absorbs oxygen at room temperature, whereas B is stable at room temperature and absorbs almost no oxygen. Both are bimolecular dimers.
6.1.1 A and B dimerize differently: A through Co-Co bonding and B through Co-O bonding. Based on this description, write the actual SMILES strings of A and B, using a textual description if necessary. The Salen ligand may be abbreviated.

6.1.2 Inactive B dissolves in certain solvents, and the resulting solution acquires the ability to absorb oxygen. [Co(II)(Salen)] dissolved in solvent S can react with oxygen by different pathways to form product C with $Co:O_2$ = 1:1 or product D with $Co:O_2$ = 2:1. The Co centers in both C and D are octahedral. Write the SMILES strings of C and D.

6.2 Inactive [Co(II)(Salen)] can be prepared as follows. Add salicylaldehyde and ethylenediamine in stoichiometric amounts successively to a three-neck flask, followed by ethanol. Yellow plate-like crystals form immediately. Assemble the apparatus shown at right, maintain the water bath at approximately 80 °C, and reflux the ethanol until the yellow crystals dissolve completely. After passing nitrogen through the two-way stopcock on the right for some time, use the syringe on the left to inject a solution of $Co(CH_3COO)_2$ slowly through the septum into the three-neck flask. Continue refluxing to obtain a dark-red crystalline precipitate. Stop heating and cool the flask in an ice-water bath while maintaining nitrogen flow and stirring. Collect the crystals on a sintered-glass funnel and dry them by suction. Wash the precipitate successively with deionized water and anhydrous ethanol, then rinse once with acetone and dry by suction to obtain dry red-brown [Co(II)(Salen)].
6.2.1 What consequences would result from adding excess ethylenediamine? State 2 consequences.
